questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: An increase in bank rate will decrease the money supply.
Lower the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), lower will be the liquidity in the system
Higher the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), lower will be the liquidity in the system.
Lower the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), higher will be the liquidity in the system.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lower the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), lower will be the liquidity in the system.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** lower Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** will actually** increase the liquidity **in the system, as banks will have **more funds** available to lend.
 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the **percentage of deposits **that banks are required to maintain with the **central bank** as a reserve.
 
• A** higher CRR** means banks have **less funds available **to lend, reducing liquidity in the system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Statutory Liquidity Ratio** (SLR) is the percentage of deposits that banks are required to maintain in the form of **liquid assets** such as **government securities. **
 
• **A lower SLR** means banks have** more funds **available to lend, increasing liquidity in the system.
 
• An **increase in bank rate,** which is the rate at which the central bank lends to commercial banks, makes borrowing more expensive for banks, **reducing **their ability to lend and **decreasing the money supply.**
 
• A** higher CRR** means banks have **less funds **available to lend,** reducing liquidity** in the system.
 
• A **lower SLR **means banks have **more funds available to lend,** increasing liquidity in the system.

questions.question: ______ is the world's largest tropical rainforest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Amazon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Amazon rainforest** covers an area of approximately** 6.7 million square kilometers** and spans across **nine countries** in South America.
 
• The Amazon rainforest is home to millions of species of **plants and animals**, making it one of the most biodiverse regions on the planet.
 
• The rainforest is also known as the **"lungs of the Earth**" as it produces more than **20% of the world's oxygen** and absorbs a significant amount of **carbon dioxide.**
 
• The Amazon rainforest is currently facing threats from **deforestation, mining, and climate change,** which could have catastrophic effects on the planet's ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prairies** are** grasslands** and not rainforests.
 
• **Daintree** is a rainforest located in **Australia**, but it is not the world's largest.
 
• **Congo **is a rainforest located in **Africa**, but it is not the world's largest either.

questions.question: Which among the following are commonly known as blood thinners?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anticoagulants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood thinners** are medications that help **prevent blood clots** from forming or getting larger.
 
• **Anticoagulants** are commonly known as **blood thinners **and are used to** treat and prevent blood clots.**
 
• **Antibiotics** are medications that are used to** treat bacterial infections.**
 
• **Anticaking** agents are substances that are added to powdered or granulated materials to **prevent clumping.**
 
• **Antibodies** are** proteins** produced by the immune system to help fight off** infections and diseases.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anticoagulants** work by interfering with the** chemical reactions i**n the body that cause blood clots to form.
 
• **Antibiotics** work by **killing or stopping **the growth of bacteria.
 
• **Anticaking** agents are commonly used in food processing to** prevent powdered or granulated materials** from clumping together.
 
• **Antibodies **are produced by **white blood cells **and are used by the immune system to **identify and neutralize harmful pathogens.**

questions.question: Which foreign invader surrendered his territories to Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seleucus Nicator.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seleucus Nicator** surrendered his territories to** Chandragupta Maurya **in around** 305 BCE**, which included parts of present-day** Afghanistan and Pakistan.**
 
• This was a significant achievement for Chandragupta Maurya as it **expanded his empire** and gave him access to important** trade routes.**
 
• **Menander,** also known as **Milinda, **was a** Greek king** who ruled over parts of present-day **Afghanistan and Pakistan** in the **2nd century BCE.**
 
 
• While he did have **interactions with the Mauryan Empire,** he **did not **surrender his territories to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
 
 
• **Demosthenes** was an **Athenian statesman** and orator who lived in the** 4th century BCE.**
 
 
• He had **no connection** to the Mauryan Empire or India.
 
 
 
• **Gondophernes **was a** Parthian ruler,** who ruled over parts of present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan in the 1st century CE, several centuries after Chandragupta Maurya.
 
 
• He also had** no **connection to the Mauryan Empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire,** one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• He ruled from around** 321 to 298 BCE **and was succeeded by his son,** Bindusara, and grandson, Ashoka.**
 
• The **Mauryan Empire **was known for its **centralized administration**, including a **sophisticated bureaucracy** and a **system of spies.**
 
• It also had a **strong military,** with **elephants **as a key component.
 
• **Seleucus Nicator **was a** Macedonian general **who served under **Alexander the Great.**
 
• After Alexander's death, he became the** ruler of the Seleucid Empire**, which included parts of present-day **Iran, Iraq, and Syria.**
 
• **Seleucus Nicator and Chandragupta Maurya** are said to have formed an alliance, with Seleucus giving his **daughter in marriage to Chandragupta** in exchange for territories in India.
 
• However, some historians question the** veracity **of this account.

questions.question: Soham is suffering from goitre. Which deficiency is the most common cause of it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deficiency of Iodine.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goitre **is a **swelling of the thyroid gland,** which is located in the neck.
 
• **Iodine deficiency** is the most common cause of goitre.
 
• Iodine is an essential nutrient that is needed for the production of** thyroid hormones.**
 
• Without enough iodine, the thyroid gland can become **enlarged **in an attempt to **produce more hormones.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein** is important for **building and repairing tissues,** and for making enzymes and hormones.
 
• A **deficiency of protein** can lead to **muscle wasting, weakened immune function,** and other health problems.
 
• **Vitamin A **is important for **vision, immune function, and skin health.**
 
• A deficiency of vitamin A can lead to** night blindness, dry skin,** and other problems.
 
• **Iron **is needed for making** hemoglobin,** which carries oxygen in the blood.
 
• A deficiency of iron can lead to** anemia, fatigue, and other symptoms.**

questions.question: Which among the following is a covalent compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen chloride.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Covalent compounds** are formed when** two or more non-metal atoms** share electrons to complete their **outermost shell.**
 
• **Hydrogen chloride** is a **covalent compound** as it is formed by the** sharing of electrons **between **hydrogen and chlorine atoms.**
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide and calcium carbonate **are both **ionic compounds**, as they are formed by the **transfer of electrons** from a metal atom (magnesium or calcium) to a non-metal atom (oxygen or hydroxide).
 
• **Sodium chloride** is also an **ionic compound,** formed by the** transfer of electrons **between sodium and chlorine atoms.
 
• **Covalent compounds** generally have** lower melting and boiling points** than ionic compounds, and are often gases or liquids at room temperature.
 
• **Hydrogen chloride **is an important** industrial chemical **used in the production of** PVC, refrigerants, and other chemicals.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium hydroxide** is an important component of **antacids** and is also used in the production of **flame retardants and wastewater treatment.**
 
• **Calcium carbonate** is found in many natural substances such as** limestone, chalk, and marble**, and is also used as a dietary supplement and in the production of **paper, plastics, and paints.**
 
• **Sodium chloride,** also known as table salt, is commonly used as a **seasoning and preservative in food**, as well as in the production o**f chemicals and textiles.**

questions.question: The Superintendence, control and conduct of all election to the municipalities is responsibility of the ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Election Commission.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Election Commission** is responsible for the **superintendence, control, and conduct **of all municipal elections in the state.
 
• This commission is a **constitutional body** that is independent of the** state government **and is responsible for ensuring **free and fair elections.**
 
• The** Governor of the State** does not have any role to play in the **conduct of municipal elections**, as this is the responsibility of the State Election Commission.
 
• The **Election Commission of India** is responsible for **conducting elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha**, and state legislative assemblies, but not for municipal elections.
 
• **The Home Ministry** of the State may have a role in providing** security and maintaining law** and order during the elections, but it is not responsible for the conduct of the elections themselves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The **State Election Commission** is a** constitutional body **established under **Article 243K **of the Constitution of India.

 
 
• Its members are appointed by the **Governor of the State**, in consultation with the **State Government **and the** State Election Commission of India.**
 
 
 
• The **Election Commission of India** is a constitutional body established under **Article 324 **of the Constitution of India.
 
 
• Its members are appointed by the** President of India.**
 
 
 
• **The Home Ministry of the State** is responsible for maintaining law and order, ensuring** public safety, and preventing and detecting crimes.**
 
 
• It is headed by the **Home Minister of the State, **who is a member of the State Cabinet.

questions.question: Which Indian cricketer is also known as 'The Wall'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rahul Dravid.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian cricketer who is also known as **'The Wall'** is **Rahul Dravid.**
 
• Dravid was given this nickname due to his **solid and dependable batting style**.
 
• He has scored over **10,000 runs** in both **Test and ODI cricket** and is considered one of the** greatest batsmen** in Indian cricket history.
 
• Dravid was also known for his excellent **slip catching **and has taken **210 catches in Test cricket,** which is a record.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kapil Dev** is a former Indian cricketer and captain who is best known for leading India to their **first-ever World Cup victory in 1983.**

 
 
• He was a** fast-bowling all-rounder **and is considered one of the** greatest players** in Indian cricket history.
 
 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar** is widely regarded as one of the **greatest batsmen **in cricket history.
 
 
• He holds numerous records, including the most runs scored in** both Test and ODI cricket**.
 
• He retired from** international cricket in 2013.**
 
 
 
• **Mahendra Singh Dhoni** is a former Indian **cricketer and captain** who is known for his calm and composed leadership style.
 
 
• He led India to multiple ICC trophies, including the **2007 T20 World Cup, the 2010 and 2016 Asia Cups, and the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup**.

questions.question: Which among the following crops is an example of Kharif crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kharif crops** are those crops which are sown in the **rainy season **and harvested in the **winter season.**
 
• **Rice** is a classic example of a Kharif crop. 
 
• **Wheat,** on the other hand, is a** Rabi crop **which is sown in the **winter season** and harvested in the summer season.
 
• **Barley** is also a **Rabi crop **which is sown in the **winter season **and harvested in the summer season.
 
• **Mustard **is a crop which is grown in both the** Rabi and Kharif seasons** depending on the region and climatic conditions.
 
• **Rice **is the** main Kharif crop **grown in India and is an important staple food for millions of people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wheat** is the second most important cereal crop after rice and is grown extensively in the **northern and central parts of India.**
 
• **Barley** is an important crop in the hilly regions of India and is used for both** human consumption and animal feed.** 
 
• **Mustard** is an oilseed crop which is grown in the **northern and eastern parts of India **and is used for making** cooking oil **and as a condiment.
 
• It is important to choose the right crop for a particular season and region as it can affect the **yield and productivity of the crop.**

questions.question: As of November 2022, who is the Speaker of Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Om Birla.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Speaker of Lok Sabha **as of **November 2022** is **Om Birla.**
 
• Om Birla is an** Indian politician** and a member of the** Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).**
 
• He was elected as the Speaker of Lok Sabha on** 19th June 2019**.
 
• Before becoming the Speaker of Lok Sabha, Om Birla was a** two-time Member of Parliament (MP)** from **Kota-Bundi constituency **in Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Droupadi Murmu** is the** current Governor** of Jharkhand.

 
 
• She was appointed as the **Governor of Jharkhand i**n** May 2015** and took the oath of office on 18th May 2015.
 
 
 
• **Narendra Modi** is the **current Prime Minister** of India.
 
 
• He was sworn in as the **Prime Minister of India on 26th May 2014** after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won the 2014 Indian general election.
 
 
 
• **Amit Shah** is a **politician and the current Union Home Minister **of India.
 
 
• He was appointed as the Union Home Minister of India on **31st May 2019** after the BJP won the 2019 Indian general election.

questions.question: Which is a major tributary of Bhagirathi river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhilangna.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhilangna** is the major tributary of **Bhagirathi river, **which is one of the two main tributaries of river Ganga.
 
• The Bhilangna river originates from the **Khatling glacier in the Garhwal region** of Uttarakhand and meets **Bhagirathi river at Old Tehri.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhauliganga **is a tributary of** Alaknanda river,** which is the other main tributary of river Ganga.
 
• It originates from the **Niti Pass in the Chamoli district **of** Uttarakhand** and joins** Alaknanda river at Vishnuprayag.**
 
• **Pindar** is also a tributary of **Alaknanda river**, which originates from the** Pindari glacier in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand** and joins Alaknanda river at Karnaprayag.
 
• **Bishenganga** is a river that flows through the states of **Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh **and joins Wainganga river, which is a tributary of **Godavari river.**

questions.question: How many UNESCO Natural World Heritage sites are there in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **seven UNESCO Natural World Heritage sites** in India.
 
• These sites are considered to be of **outstanding universal value** and are protected by** international treaties. **
 
• The seven sites are: **Kaziranga National Park, Manas Wildlife Sanctuary, Keoladeo National Park, Sundarbans National Park, Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks, Western Ghats, and Great Himalayan National Park.**
 
• These sites are chosen based on their **natural beauty, exceptional biodiversity, geological significance**, and **cultural importance.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Through international collaboration in** education, the arts, sciences, and culture, **the** United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) **works to advance **world peace and security.**
 
• It has partners in the non-governmental, intergovernmental, and private sectors in addition to its **194 member **states and **12 associate members. **
 
• **53 regional field offices **and** 199 national commissions **help UNESCO, which has its main office in **Paris, France**, carry out its global mandate.
 
• In** 1945, UNESCO **was established.
